Urgot P Echoing Flames deals damage based on your maximum health, so don’t rely on stacking health alone; also keep track of your total health so you can stay above the execute threshold. Mix in penetration because Urgot’s high armor reduces Illaoi’s physical damage.
Urgot.fight: Cast Illaoi E Test of Spirit when Urgot steps up to last-hit near a wall with tentacles. Right after he uses Urgot E Disdain, close the gap with Illaoi W Harsh Lesson to trade. Don’t follow him somewhere tentacles can’t reach, since staying near Urgot lets his leg cannons deal more damage.
Urgot.laning: When Urgot steps up to last-hit, cast Illaoi E Test of Spirit from the side with your tower and tentacles. Keep up the pressure in that area without forcing a dive.
Urgot.escape: The window to engage with Illaoi W Harsh Lesson is right after Urgot E Disdain, his mobility tool, is down. When Urgot Q Corrosive Charge is coming in, decide immediately whether to disengage with Illaoi W Harsh Lesson. If it has already hit and you can’t easily walk away, fight back where your tentacles are.
Urgot.phase: In the late game, Illaoi has less value engaging alone because she lacks reliable crowd control, so take the frontline role.

Volibear.watch: Volibear Q Thundering Smash increases his approach speed and stuns with an empowered basic attack. Wait him out beyond basic attack range, and walk sideways when you see the mark from Volibear E Sky Splitter to avoid its damage and slow. If Volibear R Stormbringer is available and your health is low, retreat deep under your tower.
Volibear.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Volibear Q Thundering Smash, W Frenzied Maul, and R Stormbringer. Buy an anti-heal item for the healing from Volibear W Frenzied Maul, and consider an item that lowers attack speed if his basic attacks are a problem. Volibear P The Relentless Storm and E Sky Splitter deal magic damage, which armor can’t block.
Volibear.fight: Don’t take a fight while Volibear is stacking Volibear P The Relentless Storm on minions. Fight near a wall with tentacles after the stacks fall off. When Volibear engages with Q Thundering Smash, cast Illaoi E Test of Spirit and counter with Illaoi R Leap of Faith on top of your tentacles. Don’t trade inconclusively and give Volibear W Frenzied Maul room to heal; if you can’t finish him, back off and wait out the cooldowns.
Volibear.laning: Cast Illaoi E Test of Spirit when Volibear steps up to last-hit, using it from the side with your tower and tentacles. Walk sideways out of the mark from Volibear E Sky Splitter.
Volibear.escape: Don’t engage just because Volibear Q Thundering Smash is down; wait for a window when Volibear R Stormbringer is also unavailable. Use Illaoi W Harsh Lesson to close the gap and fight where your tentacles are. If Volibear Q Thundering Smash is active, keep outside basic attack range and move toward your allies instead of running straight away.
Volibear.phase: In the late game, Illaoi has less value engaging alone, so focus on playing the frontline.
Volibear.teamfight: If Volibear has stacks of Volibear P The Relentless Storm, don’t take a fight immediately. Face him where your tentacles are after the stacks fall off. Pull the spirit of the nearest enemy with Illaoi E Test of Spirit, then use Illaoi R Leap of Faith to create more tentacles when the enemy engages or your allies go in. If Volibear R Stormbringer is available, don’t stay under your tower with low health.

Yone.watch: When Yone repeatedly uses Yone Q Mortal Steel on minions to prepare a whirlwind, wait out of range for the stacks to disappear. Yone R Fate Sealed pulls in enemies along its path, so don’t stand in his engage path.
Yone.build: The starting item can’t be determined from the available information alone. Yone’s damage is mixed, so don’t focus on only one resistance, and consider movement speed to get out of his telegraphed attack areas. Attack speed reduction also slows how quickly Yone Q Mortal Steel and Yone W Spirit Cleave come back.
Yone.fight: Lure Yone in near a wall with tentacles, then land Illaoi E Test of Spirit and position so you can hit both the spirit and his body. After Yone engages, counter with Illaoi R Leap of Faith and fight where your tentacles can reach. If Yone still has a mobility ability available, don’t go deep with Illaoi W Harsh Lesson first.
Yone.laning: Pull the wave toward the wall and tentacles, then cast Illaoi E Test of Spirit when Yone steps up to last-hit. Keep your distance while Yone prepares a whirlwind, then pressure him after the stacks disappear.
Yone.combo: Land Illaoi E Test of Spirit on Yone to pull his spirit, cast Illaoi Q Tentacle Smash in the direction the tentacles are facing, then close in with Illaoi W Harsh Lesson. Casting Q first lets the tentacles slam as W reaches him. In a fight where Yone engages, cast Illaoi R Leap of Faith right after pulling his spirit with E, then attack the spirit.
Yone.escape: The window to close the gap with Illaoi W Harsh Lesson is after Yone Q Mortal Steel’s whirlwind stacks disappear and Yone E Soul Unbound and R Fate Sealed are down. If only one mobility tool is down, he can still escape with the other, so don’t rush your engage.
Yone.phase: In the late game, fight from the frontline instead of engaging alone.
Yone.teamfight: Yone W Spirit Cleave gains a larger shield if it clips multiple targets, so spread out from your allies. Check your formation so you aren’t isolated at the very back of Yone R Fate Sealed’s path. If Yone engages, land Illaoi E Test of Spirit on the nearest enemy, counter with Illaoi R Leap of Faith, then attack the spirit beside the summoned tentacles.

Yorick.watch: Yorick E Mourning Mist slows, marks, and lowers resistance, so watch the mist’s trajectory and dodge it. If you’re trapped by Yorick W Dark Procession, hit the wall to break it or look for a path over it with Illaoi W Harsh Lesson. If the Maiden of the Mist starts attacking you, create distance from Yorick’s body.
Yorick.build: Build armor first against the damage from Yorick Q Last Rites and the Mist Walkers. Yorick E Mourning Mist and R Eulogy of the Isles deal magic damage based on your maximum health, so armor or health alone can’t block all of their damage.
Yorick.fight: After dodging Yorick E Mourning Mist, fight near a wall where tentacles stand, using Illaoi P Prophet of an Elder God. Yorick has no ability to create distance on his own, so close the gap with Illaoi W Harsh Lesson when you get the chance. If he has many Mist Walkers, clear them first before fighting.
Yorick.laning: Pressure Yorick with Illaoi E Test of Spirit when he steps up to last-hit. Push the wave so he can’t build graves while clearing it on his side, and make the minions die under his tower.
Yorick.combo: Damage Yorick first, then pull his spirit with Illaoi E Test of Spirit. First cast Illaoi Q Tentacle Smash in the direction the tentacles are facing, then close in with Illaoi W Harsh Lesson to chain their slams. If Yorick engages and you counter with Illaoi R Leap of Faith, pull the spirit first, cast R, then attack the spirit immediately.
Yorick.escape: After Yorick E Mourning Mist misses, you have an opportunity to step forward or engage. If Yorick uses W Dark Procession, look for a path to break the wall or go over it with Illaoi W Harsh Lesson, then engage where your tentacles can reach.
Yorick.phase: In the late game, focus on playing the frontline instead of engaging alone. Hold off Yorick’s side lane pressure, then look to join your team or trade for an objective elsewhere.
Yorick.teamfight: Land Illaoi E Test of Spirit on the nearest enemy, then cast Illaoi R Leap of Faith and attack the spirit immediately when the enemy engages or your allies go in. R creates more tentacles when enemies are grouped, so counter-engage where your tentacles are. Fight in sync with your allies’ engage so the enemy can’t scatter while your damage is high after R.

Yasuo.watch: Yasuo Q Steel Tempest has a narrow hitbox, so sidestep as he approaches instead of only backing away. The whirlwind after two hits knocks you airborne and can lead into Yasuo R Last Breath, so leave its path as soon as you hear and see the stacks reach full.
Yasuo.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Yasuo Q Steel Tempest and Yasuo R Last Breath. Armor does not reduce the magic damage from Yasuo E Sweeping Blade, and attack speed slows also delay how often the whirlwind from Yasuo Q Steel Tempest returns.
Yasuo.fight: Trigger Yasuo P Way of the Wanderer’s shield with one hit, then trade in earnest once it fades. If Yasuo dashes in through minions with Yasuo E Sweeping Blade, fight back where your tentacles can reach him, and heal with Illaoi P Prophet of an Elder God when a tentacle hits.
Yasuo.laning: Place a tentacle near a wall and pull the wave there. Cast Illaoi E Test of Spirit when Yasuo steps up to last-hit. Keep the wave thin on your side to reduce the minions Yasuo can use as stepping stones to approach with Yasuo E Sweeping Blade.
Yasuo.combo: Then close in with Illaoi W Harsh Lesson to overlap the tentacles’ slams.
Yasuo.escape: Engage right after Yasuo throws his whirlwind, when the stacks from Yasuo Q Steel Tempest reset. Yasuo E Sweeping Blade comes back quickly, so don’t chase deep just because he used it once. Look for an opening with crowd control before Yasuo R Last Breath is available again, and close the gap with Illaoi W Harsh Lesson.
Yasuo.phase: In the late game, play to counter-engage from the frontline rather than diving in alone.
Yasuo.teamfight: As your team engages, or when Yasuo dives in, cast Illaoi E Test of Spirit on the nearest enemy and immediately use Illaoi R Leap of Faith. Focus the spirit and keep enemies in an area with many tentacles to make the most of your brief window of maximum damage.
